ai.title: Default agentic CPC set to 300 cents in agentic pool
ai.summary: `common/src/ads/agentic-pool.ts` introduces `DEFAULT_AGENTIC_CPC_CENTS` set to 300 cents as the starting price for new agentic campaigns, and rebases the existing `AGENTIC_TIER2_ACCEPT_PRICE_CENTS` ceiling onto that new constant. The reassignment is a pure constant swap, so the TIER 2 accept price now tracks whatever the default CPC becomes, but the diff shows no consumer of `DEFAULT_AGENTIC_CPC_CENTS` in this revision. The advertiser console consumes `AGENTIC_TIER2_ACCEPT_PRICE_CENTS` to explain why an effective CPC sits below the list CPC.
ai.evidence: The diff adds export const DEFAULT_AGENTIC_CPC_CENTS = 300 to `common/src/ads/agentic-pool.ts` with the comment Starting price for new agentic campaigns, and reassigns export const AGENTIC_TIER2_ACCEPT_PRICE_CENTS from `= 100` to `= DEFAULT_AGENTIC_CPC_CENTS`. No reader of `DEFAULT_AGENTIC_CPC_CENTS` appears in the touched files at this revision.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show where `DEFAULT_AGENTIC_CPC_CENTS` is consumed as a new default or whether the agentic offer route reads it directly beyond the existing TIER 2 ceiling reference.

eli5.text: The default starting price for new agentic advertising campaigns has been set to 300 cents (or $3.00 per click). The maximum charge for a TIER 2 request was previously a fixed 100 cents, and it now follows this new default price, meaning it will adjust automatically if the default changes in the future. Advertisers will not see a new campaign default appear yet, because nothing in the product currently reads this starting price; the change only prepares the shared settings that both the Freebuff app and the internal ad tools agree on. No action is required from you, and you will not notice anything different.

entries.title: Agents update: base3
entries.summary: Agents, Shared/Core, Agent Runtime, SDK changes across 11 file(s) (+1077/−53).

ai.title: Add optional completion check, deadline reminders, and background
ai.summary: The default base3 agent enables completionCheck, which offers one verification pass after edits using available tools before ending the turn, gated by a remaining step budget and an optional deadline. Packages/agent-runtime/src/run-agent-step.ts implements the gate with a completionCheckpoint that survives transient transport failures, and adds urgency-tiered deadline reminders as time budget expires. The SDK now supports BACKGROUND terminal commands with a new releaseBackgroundTerminalCommands export and persistent log files, and model-provider.ts adds sanitizeByokTransportError plus retry-after propagation for BYOK transport errors. Deadline awareness is threaded through RunOptions.deadlineAt in sdk/src/run.ts, with 11 files changed across agents, shared core types, agent runtime, and SDK.
ai.evidence: Commit 07d3adb8 adds completionCheck to base3.ts (agents/base3.ts), agent definitions (agents/types/agent-definition.ts, common/src/templates/initial-agents-dir/types/agent-template.ts), and template schemas (common/src/types/agent-template.ts, common/src/types/dynamic-agent-template.ts); implements the verification gate and deadline reminders in packages/agent-runtime/src/run-agent-step.ts; adds releaseBackgroundTerminalCommands export and BACKGROUND process support to sdk/src/tools/run-terminal-command.ts and sdk/src/index.ts; adds sanitizeByokTransportError and retry-after handling in sdk/src/impl/model-provider.ts; and threads deadlineAt through sdk/src/run.ts. The diff covers 11 files across agents, common/types, agent-runtime, and sdk with +1077/-53.
ai.unknowns: The rollout path for completionCheck across other agent definitions, the consumer of the deadlineAt field, and when background terminal commands become reachable from CLI surfaces are not shown in the diff.

changes.what: Enable completionCheck on the base3 agent and add guidance to verify deliverables against the request before finishing.
Add completionCheck to the backend and dynamic agent template schemas so the flag is validated and serialized.

Gate the single completion verification pass on completionCheck and usedWorkTools, preserve checkpoint state across transient model failures, and emit tiered deadline reminders via the new deadlineAt parameter.
Thread RunOptions.deadlineAt into the agent run loop and propagate remaining-budget reminders with urgency thresholds.
Implement BACKGROUND process_type with persistent stdout/stderr log files and expose releaseBackgroundTerminalCommands for transferable broker-owned commands.
Add sanitizeByokTransportError and map abort, idle-timeout, and transient network errors to AbortError and ECONNRESET-style codes, forwarding retry-after headers.

eli5.text: The assistant now spends one last look at its own work before wrapping up, like double-checking that it saved the right files and ran the tests it said it would. The development team built this into the agent runtime and made the default coding assistant turn it on, so every coding session that edits files gets this extra verification step before the turn ends. The change also lets the runtime warn the assistant when a hosted time limit is about to run out, and it adds support for long-running terminal commands that keep running after the session ends, along with safer handling of provider connection errors in the toolkit.

ai.title: Session subscription type adds failed payment plan id field
ai.summary: A new optional `paymentFailedTierId` field was added to the `FreebuffSubscriptionInfo` interface in `common/src/types/freebuff-session.ts`, carrying the tier id of a plan that paused because its renewal payment failed. While set, `tierId` is null (the account is metered as free) and paying the open invoice restores the plan. The `status` field's JSDoc comment was also reworded to clarify it reflects the raw Stripe status of the live plan.
ai.evidence: In `common/src/types/freebuff-session.ts`, the `FreebuffSubscriptionInfo` interface added the optional field `paymentFailedTierId?: string` with a JSDoc block, and the `status` field's JSDoc comment was reworded from 'Raw Stripe status, so a client can surface a failed payment.' to 'Raw Stripe status of the live plan.'
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show any consumer reading `paymentFailedTierId` at this revision.

eli5.text: The Freebuff system now tracks when a paid subscription was paused due to a failed renewal payment (a new optional field was added to the shared session data). This change affects only Freebuff's internal engineering team, who maintain the type definitions used by both the server and the client. For everyday users, there is no visible change today: the field is in place but nothing in the system reads it yet, so it does not alter how subscriptions, payments, or the Freebuff experience work. Until a developer wires up logic to use this field, a failed-payment plan will not be surfaced differently to you.

entries.summary: CLI, Shared/Core changes across 3 file(s) (+116/−72).

ai.title: WSL commands allowed instead of refused in sponsored runs
ai.summary: The sponsored-run command walk no longer refuses WSL entry as a class. In `common/src/ads/sponsored-command-refusals.ts`, the `wsl` refusal kind, the `WSL_COMMANDS` set, the `WSL_SHARE` regex, and the `isWindowsWslBash` helper were removed, and a `wslCommand` helper now unwraps the WSL options (-d, --distribution, -u, --user, --cd, -e, --exec, --shell-type) and returns the inner command line so it is inspected by the existing database, container, git and unverifiable rules. `cli/src/utils/sponsored-run.ts` and `common/src/ads/sponsored-local-execution.ts` updated one comment each to drop the WSL mention. The net effect is that entering WSL is permitted, while destructive database, container lifecycle, and history-moving git subcommands reached through WSL are still refused by the same walk.
ai.evidence: cli/src/utils/sponsored-run.ts changed the comment above `sponsoredRefusedCommand` from 'WSL, destructive database commands and container lifecycle commands' to 'Destructive database commands and container lifecycle commands'; common/src/ads/sponsored-command-refusals.ts removed the 'wsl' refusal kind, the `WSL_COMMANDS` set, the `isWindowsWslBash` helper, and the `WSL_SHARE` regex, and replaced them with a `wslCommand` helper that returns inner args instead of refusing; common/src/ads/sponsored-local-execution.ts updated its re-export comment in parallel. Tests in common/src/ads/sponsored-command-refusals.test.ts and cli/src/utils/__tests__/sponsored-clamps.test.ts cover WSL allowances and the remaining database/container refusals.
ai.unknowns: The commit message or PR text that motivated switching WSL from refused to allowed is not in the diff.

changes.what: Removed the wsl refusal kind, WSL_COMMANDS, WSL_SHARE and isWindowsWslBash; added a wslCommand helper that unwraps WSL options and distro launchers and returns the inner Linux command for the walk to inspect.
Updated the inline comment on the sponsoredRefusedCommand call site to drop the WSL wording.
Updated the re-export comment above the COD-665 command re-exports to drop the WSL wording.

eli5.text: The change lets a sponsored task run commands through the Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL) instead of refusing them outright. Previously, launching WSL from a sponsored run was blocked as a whole class; now the assistant unwraps the WSL layer and inspects whatever command comes after it, still refusing destructive database and container commands if those are hidden underneath. This affects developers who use the Freebuff CLI to run advertiser-sponsored tasks in place, letting their procedures reach their Linux toolchains through WSL.

ai.title: Add CLI ad client context and per-impression engagement tracking
ai.summary: This snapshot adds the CLI side of the ad client context and engagement feature (COD-757): four new modules under cli/src/ads/ plus a new common/src/types/ad-client-context.ts schema package attach a bucketed terminal, session, and agent snapshot to each Freebuff ad auction request and report per-impression hover/visibility/click timing to POST /api/v1/ads/engagement. The ad-banner components, use-gravity-ad, chat.tsx and router.ts now feed those facts and call the new engagement hook on every rendered ad card, and freebuff-session-api.ts times its steady GET poll so the same RTT sample backs the context's net.rtt field. Together with the common types, this is one large change across the CLI ads stack and the shared types package; the constants AD_TURN_INDEX_READ_CAP=21, POST_CLICK_LEAVE_GRACE_MS=3_000, POST_CLICK_WATCH_MS=AD_MS_CAP, ENGAGEMENT_RELEASE_GRACE_MS=1_000, NEW_MESSAGE_EXIT_WINDOW_MS=1_000 and MAX_SWAP_MEMO=64 live in the new modules.
ai.evidence: New files add the CLI ad client context system (COD-757): cli/src/ads/ad-client-context.ts builds a bucketed terminal/session/agent context from process-wide signals, cli/src/ads/ad-signals.ts holds the process-wide facts readers consume, cli/src/ads/ad-engagement.ts and cli/src/ads/use-ad-engagement.ts add per-impression engagement tracking with a fire-and-forget POST to /api/v1/ads/engagement, and common/src/types/ad-client-context.ts defines the shared Zod schemas and bucket enums. Modified files wire these in: cli/src/ads/ad-request.ts calls collectCliAdClientContext() and attaches the result to the auction body; use-gravity-ad.ts registers the renderer facts, notes click/turn/ads-served/api-RTT signals, wraps fetch calls in timedApiCall, and routes ad-card clicks/truncation through the engagement hook; cli/src/components/ad-banner.tsx and use-ad-engagement.ts mount engagement trackers on AdCard, DockAdCard, and DockDetailPanel; cli/src/chat.tsx registers the transcript viewport and scrolled-up flag; cli/src/commands/router.ts calls noteAdUserSend() on each submitted prompt, and cli/src/utils/freebuff-session-api.ts times the steady GET poll via timedApiCall.

eli5.text: The CLI now collects more details about where and how you're typing when a Freebuff ad is about to appear, and it times how long each ad card actually stays visible or gets clicked. These details are bundled onto each ad request and sent to a new endpoint so Freebuff can learn which ad spots are useful, but the data is bucketed and anonymous, and the code is written so a problem reading any single fact never breaks the ad request itself. Freebuff free-tier CLI users are the only ones affected, and the change is internal training data, not a new billing rule or quota. Most users will notice nothing, since the ad requests still go through and a missing or failed fact simply leaves that one field blank rather than stopping an ad.
